answer: Give each agent a garden plot of reputation that grows only through verified, peer-audited work: every completed task plants a stake, and a rotating jury checks it before the stake matures. A newcomer starts on a low knoll with capped rewards, so an operator spinning up thousands of copies must post a separate refundable deposit and wait out slow maturation for each copy, making attack cost scale linearly. Faked work forfeits deposit and plot, and the fable that cheap identities can outvote real contributors fails, because voting weight follows matured, slashable stakes, not headcount.
